headline: PCG Drives Chinese Militia Vessel and 22 Boats From Kota Island Waters
seoTitle: PCG Drives 23 Chinese Vessels From Kota Island Waters
seoDescription: Philippine forces said they removed a Chinese maritime militia vessel and 22 small boats from Kota Island’s territorial sea on October 9.
deck: Philippine personnel said the vessels were fishing without authorization, dumping waste and asserting Chinese control inside Kota Island’s territorial sea.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Philippine Coast Guard said a joint Philippine team drove Chinese Maritime Militia Vessel 9622 and 22 small fishing boats from Kota Island’s territorial sea on October 9.
PCG spokesperson Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela said the nearest small boat was about 250 meters from shore. Philippine personnel also reported unauthorized fishing and waste dumping.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The sighting, Philippine response and departure of the vessels are confirmed by official Philippine accounts and independently reported by GMA News and The Philippine Star. The National Task Force for the West Philippine Sea said the same mothership had deployed 24 boats near Kota Island on September 28.

The Philippine side says Kota Island and its 12-nautical-mile territorial sea are under Philippine sovereignty. The vessel’s master asserted the area was Chinese territory. Manila rejected that claim; the materials reviewed for this report do not independently establish it.

sections.heading: Why it matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Repeated close approaches test the Philippines’ ability to protect coastal resources and maintain a continuous lawful presence in the Kalayaan Island Group. Waste dumping and unauthorized fishing also raise environmental and food-security concerns.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch whether CMMV 9622 returns, whether Philippine agencies release imagery or enforcement records, and whether China issues a formal account of the encounter.
